name: I Am Caribbean (2020)
description: White with 'Caribbean' in big magenta letters over the forward windows and again along the belly. The hummingbird fills the aft half of the fin in bright streaks. A broad red feather sits among mauve and pink ones banded in yellow, lime and sky blue, and its orange and crimson tail runs under the tailplane onto the tail cone. Magenta engines and winglets, gray wings and tailplane. The registration is small in dark purple aft.

logos.description: Caribbean Airlines' hummingbird as redrawn for the 2020 brand: a fan of long tapering feather streaks rising toward the fin's tip by its trailing edge, a broad red one at the heart among mauve and pink ones, thin yellow, lime and pale sky-blue streaks between them, white fin showing between the feathers; a band of short slanted streaks (red, sky, yellow, lime, pink on mauve) along the fin's foot running forward over the fillet; the orange and crimson tail spills under the tailplane onto the tail cone. The leading half of the fin stays white. The areas carry its major color fields; the streaks are the artwork's.

titles.style: The 2020 wordmark: heavy geometric sans in mixed case with round bowls and a large x-height, magenta, over the forward windows from just behind the forward door. 'Airlines' isn't on the aircraft.
The same wordmark, larger, along the belly ahead of the wing, reading nose to tail from below.
The aircraft's own registration in dark purple capitals under the last windows ahead of the aft door; 'BOEING 737-8' in small italic capitals above the windows there isn't drawn.

AT76.note: The ATR 72-600s, measured on 9Y-TTF (right side from below, 2024-10-16) fitted to shapes/AT76.json by its windows, aft door and the body's depth, so the lettering keeps its place by the windows (the shape's cabin and nacelle sit about 1.1 to 1.4 m forward of where photos put them against the nose and tail); 9Y-TTG and 9Y-TTH (left, 2023), 9Y-TTA and 9Y-TTC (2025) agree. The title is smaller and sits higher, from the forward exit back over the propeller's arc. A ribbon picture of the hummingbird in thin rainbow lines runs along the window line from just behind the exit to the aft door. The registration is magenta italic over the aft windows. The fin art and the tail cone's colors are drawn as on the 737. The tail cone's mauve is kept below the dorsal fillet, which runs far forward on the ATR and shows only the logo's streaks in photos.

A long hummingbird drawn in loose thin rainbow ribbons (red, orange, purple, magenta, yellow, lime, sky blue) flowing along and through the window line, its head and beak toward the tail. It runs about 13 m, from just behind the forward exit to the aft door; the windows show through it.

notes: Measured on the 737 MAX 8 from 9Y-CAL (left, level, 2026-02-18) fitted to shapes/B38M.json, checked on 9Y-ANT (right, 2025-11-20), 9Y-JAM (2025), 9Y-BAH (2024) and 9Y-TTO (2022). 'Caribbean' runs x 0.171 to 0.352 just over the windows, its capitals about 0.8 m tall and its lowercase 0.78 of them. The right side carries it over the same stretch. The belly title was read off photos from below (9Y-BAR, 9Y-JAM) and its run is estimated. The hummingbird is the airline's artwork. The fin's areas carry its major color fields (redrawn 2026-11-27 from 9Y-CAL as the feathers' outlines: the red, mauve and pink feathers; the band of streaks along the foot is the logo's alone, as an area it would run far forward along an ATR's long fillet) and the tail cone's orange and crimson; its many thin yellow, lime and sky-blue streaks stay the logo's. The art faces the same way on both sides. Small 'BOEING 737-8' lettering over the aft windows and a small decal under 9Y-JAM's cockpit in 2023 aren't drawn. The ATR 72-600s wear the scheme too, with their own title, registration and a ribbon hummingbird along the windows (`types`, AT76). The 737-800s weren't measured. No open photo shows one in this scheme. When it was unveiled in 2020 the twelve 737-800s were said unlikely to be repainted, and the newest open photo of one (9Y-JME, 2019) shows the 2007 scheme. So a 737-800 drawn in this scheme may be wrong.
history: New. Replaced the 2007 scheme (white with red-to-purple script 'Caribbean Airlines' titles and the first hummingbird on the fin). It was first shown on ATR 72-600 9Y-TTI in March 2020 and came with the 737 MAX 8s delivered from early 2022 (9Y-BAH in February 2022). Some 2007-scheme aircraft flew on after that (ATR 9Y-TTB in December 2022).
